projectMove.title: Cruise: knock out online check-in today
projectMove.body: Carnival online check-in opens this morning, and finishing it early gets you the best Arrival Appointment, since the earliest windows around 10 to 11 AM go first. It takes about fifteen minutes in the Carnival Planner under My To-do List, and the hard deadline is midnight on October 31, the same night the Tallahassee bus leaves, so doing it today removes the last-minute risk entirely.

tip.title: Have three things ready before you open check-in
tip.body: Keep your government photo ID, an emergency contact name and phone number, and a clear, well-lit photo of your face handy before you start, because the form asks for all three and stalls without them. Also, tonight drops to about 50F, so grab a layer if you step out after Russian.

ottoman.chapterTitle: Chapter 14: The end of the caliphate
ottoman.summary: When the sultanate was abolished in November 1922, the Ankara assembly kept a separate caliphate and named Abdülmecid II caliph without making him sultan. That arrangement proved unstable, and on 3 March 1924 the Turkish assembly abolished the caliphate and expelled the Ottoman dynasty. The decision grounded the new republic's sovereignty in national institutions while leaving a wider argument about religious authority, from British India's Khilafat movement onward, unresolved.

surprise.title: The day a Parisian cat went to space
surprise.body: On October 18, 1963, a Paris street cat later known as Félicette rode a French Véronique rocket to become the first cat ever launched into space. She was one of 14 cats trained for the program, wore sensors that tracked her brain activity the whole way up, and her capsule was recovered just 13 minutes after liftoff. Four years later on this exact date, in 1967, the Soviet probe Venera 4 became the first spacecraft to directly measure the atmosphere of another planet, Venus. October 18 has quietly been a big day for space.
